Rationale.DE1_ResultFidelity: The replicated results match the original within acceptable tolerance. The original reports peak effects at layers 15-18 with AIE=6.6% for MLP vs 1.6% for attention; the replication reports layers 15-20 with MLP recovery ~60-70% vs attention ~20-30%. Both identify the last subject token as critical. Layer ranges show excellent agreement (15-20 vs 15-18) within expected experimental variance, and the MLP/attention dominance pattern is consistently reproduced.
Rationale.DE2_ConclusionConsistency: The replicated documentation presents conclusions fully consistent with the original. Both conclude that factual associations are localized in middle-layer MLP modules, the last subject token is the critical position, MLPs dominate over attention in causal importance, and MLP layers act as key-value associative memories. No contradictions or meaningful differences in interpretation were found.
Rationale.DE3_NoExternalInformation: No external or hallucinated information was introduced. All content in the replicated documentation traces back to: (1) original repository files (plan.md, CodeWalkthrough.md, source code), (2) standard model specifications from HuggingFace, (3) the replication's own verified experimental outputs, and (4) the original paper citation. No invented findings or unsupported claims were detected.
